reply_text:
I read this as **pass, coverage only**. The reporter's sentence is on the page word for word, but it is a news report paraphrasing Lee, not his own words.

**1. The page.** It opened. It is a Caixin Global article by Yang Zirui, "Kai-Fu Lee Says AI Will Soon Reshape Corporate Reporting and Management", published 22 July 2026 at 12:08 a.m. GMT+8. Its first paragraph matches the candidate exactly: "Kai-Fu Lee, the prominent tech investor and founder of 01.AI, expects artificial intelligence to fundamentally reshape large companies' financial reporting and management structures within the next year." That sentence is the reporter's. The article then says this came from an exclusive interview with Caixin at the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference. Only those two paragraphs are open; the rest is behind a paywall, so I could not see any direct quote from Lee.

The page also has an "AI generated" summary box. It reads "within the next year" as 2027 and lists two other forecasts from the same interview, both paraphrased:
- Companies that don't adapt "risk becoming obsolete within three years". This is also in the open second paragraph.
- Middle management will shrink and hierarchies flatten over three to five years. This appears only in the summary box.

Neither of these is part of this candidate. They might be worth separate candidates, but they too would be coverage only.

**2. The four parts of the rule.**
- **Part 1, role: met.** In July 2026 Lee was the founder of 01.AI, which builds models. That is the role his other 2026 recorded claims were admitted under.
- **Part 2, about AI and forward-looking: met.** It says AI will reshape large companies' financial reporting and management structures. That is a claim about what AI will do, not a spending or revenue forecast. "Fundamentally reshape" is vague, though. When the bar is written, the claim may well be judged `unfalsifiable`, but that is decided at entry, not under this rule.
- **Part 3, date: met.** "Within the next year" is a span counted from the day it was said, so it is due in 2027.
- **Part 4, primary source: met only as coverage.** The only source is the news report's paraphrase, and the paywalled text may or may not hold a direct quote.

**3. Already recorded?** No. None of the listed claim files is about corporate reporting or management within a year. The nearest, the 2026-09-04 file on AI changing jobs in five years, is a different claim.

**Date:** the page gives only the publication date, 22 July 2026. The interview was at the conference shortly before, so the year and month (2026-07) are firm but the exact day is not.
